hint: a convenience store — open 24h, on nearly every Korean block
24 hours; 24시간 영업 = open around the clock
a display stand or shelf unit in a shop
use-by date — replaced 유통기한 on Korean labels in 2023; the date it is safe to eat until
a part-time worker; 편의점 알바 is the classic Korean student job
the window counter seat where you eat what you just bought
a microwave — free for customers to use in the store
the hot water dispenser, for cup ramen
dropping off a parcel — Korean convenience stores double as courier counters
sold out; 품절이에요 = we're out of that
the checkout counter
a bag — 봉투 드릴까요? is the first question at any Korean counter
a plastic bag — no longer free; you pay per bag
the official volume-rate rubbish bag; you must buy your district's own, and convenience stores sell them
accruing points; 적립하시겠어요? = shall I add your points?
a cash receipt registered to your phone number, for tax deduction
paying in one lump sum, as opposed to 할부 (instalments) — you'll be asked which
1+1, buy one get one free — written 1+1 and read out this way
an item on promotion
change (money returned)
a barcode; 바코드 찍다 = to scan it
a boxed meal — the convenience-store 도시락 is a full cheap dinner, a staple for students and office workers
a triangular rice ball in seaweed; note the wrapper opening order printed 1-2-3
cup ramen — filled at the store's hot water dispenser and eaten on the spot
to heat something up (in a microwave)
'Shall I heat it up for you?' — asked about any hot-case or boxed item
disposable wooden chopsticks, taken from the counter bin
a lid — 뚜껑을 덮다 = to put the lid on (while ramen steeps)
the soup powder sachet inside instant ramen (from 'soup', but means the packet)
fish cake — sold hot on skewers by the counter in winter
the heated display case keeping drinks and buns warm — the winter counterpart to the fridge
a rice meal in a cup, microwaved at the store
a food delivery app (배달의민족, 쿠팡이츠 and the like)
the delivery fee, charged on top of the food and shown before you pay
the minimum order amount a shop will deliver for
the request box — where you type notes for the restaurant or the driver
disposables (cutlery, napkins); 일회용품 빼주세요 = please leave them out
a review event — free extra food in exchange for writing a review
bundled delivery — the driver drops other orders on the way, so it costs less but arrives later
takeout ordered through the app and picked up yourself, usually with no fee
a star rating; 별점 테러 = tanking a shop's rating out of spite
a coupon applied at checkout

term: 문 앞에 두고 벨 눌러 주세요
hint: 'Leave it at the door and ring the bell' — the single most-typed delivery request in Korea
the shared entrance door code for an apartment building, which drivers need to get in
'Please don't ring the bell' — written when a baby is asleep or you're on a call
the respectful way to address a delivery driver (literally 'driver, sir/ma'am')
contact-free — 비대면 배달 means it's left at the door with no face-to-face handover
the door handle; 문고리에 걸어 주세요 = please hang it on the handle
'delivery complete' — the app's final status notification
the estimated arrival time shown on the app's tracking screen
